newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudi barley price range $163.50-173.50 - traders.
newsitem.headline: Saudi barley price range $163.50-173.50 - traders.

text.p: Saudi Arabia has pencilled in a purchase of 700,000 tonnes of optional-origin barley from the world market at prices ranging from $163.50 to $173.50 per tonne c and f, European grain traders said on Tuesday.

The deals, initially seen at $164 to $171 a tonne, still lacked official confirmation but were expected to be finalised soon, though offers must stay valid for two weeks, they said. Traders said the updated range of prices corresponded to average fob prices of $143 to $153 per tonne.
Canadian trade sources said earlier the deals included a minimum 150,000 tonnes of barley at $145 a tonne to be sold fob Vancouver. The Canadian Wheat Board declined to comment.

Several European traders said the European Union, near the end of its current campaign, was expected to supply 150,000 to 200,000 tonnes towards the purchase, although one put the target for EU origin around 100,000 tonnes higher.
U.S. barley seemed included, though this may not rule out late delivery penalties being built in to the cost, traders said. The barley was due for arrival by July 15.

One source said four companies had clinched the deal, the second major Saudi barley purchase in a month. The kingdom bought 500,000 tonnes of feed barley in April at prices estimated between $152 and $154 per tonne including freight for delivery in April and May.
